assignment_rule: A neuron's family is the family holding the majority of its connections; a neuron with no majority family (fresh, or scrambled by a per-connection crossover) draws one weighted by its own connections per eligible family, i.e. for a fresh uniform neuron P(family) = the family's share of the encoded bits ('my first connection picks the family'). Aggregate wiring per family therefore matches spread; only its concentration changes.
fallback: A family is a HOME for a w-bit neuron only if it has at least w - floor(rf_cross*w) distinct ENCODED bits (after ids_encoding_dedupe, if on). A smaller family is reachable at that width only through the cross budget; a neuron whose width no family can host is exempt (left as drawn). Nothing is ever placed out-of-family to cover a deficit, so a projected neuron's family always holds a strict majority of its connections (rf_cross < 0.5).
notes: Rates (Flow Packets/s, ...) join timing rather than a family of their own: they are counts over the flow duration, and on the legacy list a rate family would be one feature.
port is one feature: a home only for neurons narrower than its encoded width + budget; otherwise reachable via the cross budget.

size.why: Bidirectional packet-size statistics and the down/up ratio: the shape of the packets regardless of direction.

bwd_size.why: What the RESPONDER sent: backward packet sizes, totals, subflow and bulk statistics.

fwd_size.why: What the INITIATOR sent: forward packet sizes, totals, subflow, payload-carrying packets and bulk statistics.

header_window.why: TCP header fields: initial windows, header lengths, minimum segment size and the flag counters (set by the TCP stack, not by the payload).

timing.why: Time structure: flow / forward / backward inter-arrival times, active and idle periods, duration, and the per-second rates derived from duration.
